summary: Dippu Singh leads emerging data technologies and AI architecture at Fujitsu North America. He presents a deep dive into engineering a low-latency voice intelligence pipeline for contact centers, where audio data starts messy—overlapping, emotionally charged, and multi-channel—unlike the clean text inputs generative AI typically handles. The motivation is structural breakdown in contact centers: over 50% identify hiring, training, and productivity as critical barriers, with high stress driving turnover and creating a negative spiral of understaffing. The most glaring inefficiency is after-call work (ACW), where a 6.5-minute average call generates 6.3 minutes of post-processing, nearly a 1:1 ratio, with inconsistent data quality due to reliance on operator memory and writing skills. The engineering mission targets mechanizing summarization and data extraction to reduce post-processing by 50% or more. The four-stage pipeline begins with voice capture: real-time audio intake with noise filtering, level normalization, and critical stereo channel mapping to isolate agent and customer. A security layer applies early-stage PII masking so sensitive data never reaches LLM memory. Stage two is speech-to-text (STT), requiring above 90% accuracy, using advanced acoustic modeling for phoneme mapping and dialect filtering, domain-specific dictionaries for vocabulary disambiguation, and inverse text normalization for numerical formatting. Stage three is the generative AI core, using an orchestration layer with specific prompt templates and few-shot libraries to produce structured bullet points rather than narrative paragraphs. A reasoning layer extracts intent from a predefined list of call reasons with classification justification. A trust layer applies token optimization for low latency and automated hallucination checks. Stage four is customer data sync, where an API gateway maps JSON output to CRM fields via REST APIs. A human verification step remains: operators review AI-generated summaries, make minor edits, and confirm. Structured data also flows into business intelligence models for management dashboards and FAQ candidate flagging. Deployment outcomes show ACW time dropping from 6.3 to 3.1 minutes, a 50% reduction, yielding operational savings equivalent to reclaiming dozens of full-time headcounts across 500 seats. Data entry quality shifted from subjective and variable to standardized, consistent output, reducing cognitive load on operators and directly combating stress-linked turnover. Three main constraints remain: STT accuracy with heavy accents and poor audio, initial API token costs for long transcripts, and security compliance overhead from PII masking layers that increase latency. The roadmap has three phases: explainable AI for post-call operator coaching on soft skills and empathy, predictive staffing using categorized intent data fed into time-series analytics for call volume forecasting and shift optimization, and real-time acoustic and sentiment analysis to detect customer harassment and protect agent mental health through supervisor alerts or seamless transfer to AI voice agents.

sections.title: Introduction and Problem Context
sections.summary: Dippu Singh introduces the session on low-latency intelligence extraction from messy audio streams, contrasting clean text inputs with real-world contact center audio that is overlapping, emotionally charged, and multi-channel. He outlines the roadmap: current challenges, solution architecture, key outcomes, and roadmap ahead.

sections.title: Contact Center Operational Challenges
sections.summary: Contact centers face structural breakdown with over 50% citing hiring, training, and productivity as critical barriers. High stress drives turnover, creating a negative spiral of understaffing. The most glaring inefficiency is after-call work (ACW): 6.5-minute calls generate 6.3 minutes of post-processing, a near 1:1 ratio, with inconsistent data quality. The engineering mission targets mechanizing summarization to reduce post-processing by 50%.

sections.title: Four-Stage Pipeline Architecture Overview
sections.summary: Singh introduces the four-stage low-latency pipeline: voice capture for raw audio extraction, speech-to-text for transcription, generative AI core for intent recognition and summarization, and customer data sync for CRM updates via API calls.

sections.title: Stage 1: Voice Capture
sections.summary: Voice capture applies noise filtering, audio normalization, and critical stereo channel mapping to isolate agent and customer on separate channels. A security layer uses buffer management and early-stage PII masking so sensitive data like credit card numbers never reaches LLM memory banks.

sections.title: Stage 2: Speech-to-Text Engine
sections.summary: STT requires above 90% accuracy using advanced acoustic modeling for phoneme mapping and dialect filtering. Domain-specific dictionaries disambiguate similar terms. Inverse text normalization and auto punctuation convert spoken formats like $5,000 into numerical representations, improving downstream entity extraction.

sections.title: Stage 3: Generative AI Core
sections.summary: The generative AI core uses an orchestration layer with prompt templates and few-shot libraries to produce structured bullet points rather than narrative. A reasoning layer extracts intent from predefined call reasons with classification justification. A trust layer applies token optimization for low latency and automated hallucination checks for grounding.

sections.title: Stage 4: Customer Data Sync and Linear Workflow
sections.summary: An API gateway maps JSON output to CRM fields via REST APIs. Human verification remains: operators review, edit, and confirm AI summaries. Structured data flows into BI models for dashboards and FAQ flagging. The linear workflow processes transcripts through speaker separation, context deduction with entity extraction and sentiment analysis, and structured JSON output.

sections.title: Deployment Outcomes
sections.summary: ACW time dropped from 6.3 minutes to 3.1 minutes, approximately 50% reduction. Across 500 seats handling thousands of calls daily, savings equal reclaiming dozens of full-time headcounts. Data entry quality shifted from subjective and variable to standardized and uniform output, with improved call reason tagging.

sections.title: Engineering Constraints and Future Roadmap
sections.summary: Three main constraints remain: STT accuracy with heavy accents and poor audio quality, initial API token costs for complex LLM reasoning on long 20-minute transcripts, and security compliance overhead from PII masking layers that increase latency. The roadmap has three phases: phase one focuses on explainable AI for post-call operator coaching on soft skills and empathy; phase two targets predictive staffing by feeding categorized intent data into time-series analytics for call volume forecasting and shift optimization; phase three aims to combat customer harassment through low-latency sentiment and acoustic analysis that detects abuse and triggers supervisor alerts or seamless transfer to AI voice agents to protect operator mental health.
